correctness.rationale: Starting solely from the two exact clauses of Ostrovsky Main Theorem 1 (linear weight-doubling tau and isolation of ALL completed-code vectors of weight<=H as tau(C)), the binary support identity sum_(u in U) wt(u)=2^(r-1)|Supp(U)| follows because every active coordinate evaluates as a nonzero linear functional on an r-space. Hence tau doubles support size of every r-subcode. Because every vector of a completed-code subcode D with support<=H has weight<=H, D is contained in tau(C) and corresponds uniquely to a source subcode, proving the whole bounded-support spectrum bijection. A source minimizer maps into short support <=2m<=H; any completed-code minimizer must therefore be an image, giving exact d_r(A)=2d_r(C) for 1<=r<=dim C. This does not assert higher completed-code weights or establish the existence of the host independently of the published theorem. Independently checked binary support-sum for all 67 F2^4 subspaces and representative surrogate spectra; the finite surrogate is not the self-dual completion.
residual_risks: Entire theorem conditional on source construction and its exact low-weight isolation clause, not self-dual construction independently reproduced.
Only r<=dim C; larger host weights and different host completions beyond cutoff not determined.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary Ostrovsky theorem explicitly isolates short vectors and doubles individual weights, and derives minimum distance; it does not itself state the bounded-support subcode bijection and entire generalized Hamming hierarchy. Classical Wei generalized weights and later design-specific higher-weight spectra do not supply that completion-specific consequence. The support identity is standard and could be viewed as an elementary corollary of the source, so the accepted novelty is the explicit structural all-r support-spectrum implication, not a new completion, isometry principle or foundational lemma.
residual_risks: Potential implicit corollary of already published strong weight-doubling plus low-weight isolation; priority beyond explicit theorem statement is modest and may have been noted elsewhere.
No new statements about generalized weights above dim(C).

value.rationale: A full bounded-support subcode spectrum is a natural invariant of the new metric self-dual embedding and determines all source generalized Hamming weights within the host, far richer than just d1. Its all-r bijection and exact support multiplicities can be used for enumerative coding, secret sharing and higher-weight analysis of completed self-dual codes. This is a motivated reusable structural corollary, not an arbitrary small numeric computation; short proof is acknowledged.
